DOI: 10.1126/scitranslmed.aat7467 Drug repurposing helps iron out porphyria Porphyria is an inherited incurable disorder resulting from the buildup of heme precursors throughout the body. Urquiza et al. showed that ciclopirox, already approved as an antifungal, allosterically stabilized a mutated biosynthetic enzyme (uroporphyrinogen III synthase or UROIIIS) that leads to this condition. Oral ciclopirox administration increased UROIIIS activity and reduced clinical symptoms in a mouse model of porphyria. Further work will be needed to show whether ciclopirox is suitable for chronic treatment. The authors' drug repurposing pipeline could potentially be co-opted to investigate therapies for other enzyme mutations that cause metabolic disease.
